title: Probe-gating caused under-scale during burst: root cause and remediation plan
creator: Asha Menon
description: This ticket documents the follow-up and action items for a capacity regression on 2026-03-09 where the KEDA-triggered HPA did not scale fast enough during a traffic spike, causing elevated latencies and limited throughput. The investigation focused on probe gating logic, metrics aggregation windowing, and trigger sensitivity for bursty workloads.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 at 03:12 UTC a burst of traffic to hosted inference endpoints caused sustained latencies above SLO for ~18 minutes. Autoscaler did not provision sufficient replicas quickly because KEDA's event scaling was gated by a probe-based damping heuristic that suppressed trigger counts for short high-frequency bursts. The suppression prevented target pods from reaching the needed count before downstream request queues backed up.
timeline: 2026-03-09 03:12 - Traffic spike begins; 03:14 - 95th p95 latency crosses 350ms; 03:18 - ops alerted via SLO monitor; 03:20 - emergency scaling policy applied (manual override) and burst capacity enabled; 03:30 - traffic recedes and latencies return to normal. Post-incident investigation run 03/10-03/12.
root_cause: The autoscaling stack relied on a probe gating mechanism intended to suppress noisy trigger events from transient probes. During a sustained short-duration burst (~2m) the gating window aggregated events and treated them as noise, lowering effective trigger rate to KEDA. Additionally, a recent change to metric windowing (reduced to 15s for cost reasons) made the signal less granular for short bursts. The combination resulted in false negatives: the HPA thought demand was lower than actual.
mitigations: Reverted probe-gating default to previous behavior for burst-sensitivity (roll back the damping parameter set in runtime-1.22)
Temporarily extended metric aggregation window to 45s for high-throughput endpoints to improve short-burst fidelity
Added an EmergencyOverride policy to enable fast manual scale to reserved capacity in the event of SLO breaches
Updated alerting to include a replicated metric (queue depth) that bypasses probe-gating and triggers runbook checks
action_items: ENG: Implement adaptive probe-gating that distinguishes sustained bursts from probe noise (owner: Luca) - estimate 5
ENG: Add percentile-based KEDA trigger in addition to rate-based trigger to detect burst demand (owner: Mei Chen) - estimate 3
ENG: Run load tests that simulate 30-90s burst patterns across endpoint classes and record autoscaler responsiveness (owner: SRE team) - estimate 2
PM: Update customer communication template for capacity incidents and include time-to-scale expectations (owner: Priya Patel) - estimate 1
Docs: Add a guidance doc on when to apply modified aggregation windows and per-endpoint policies (owner: Developer Experience) - estimate 2
follow_up_tasks: Champion a new autoscale policy matrix mapping endpoint class -> aggregation window -> gating params
Schedule a canary of adaptive probe-gating on a low-risk customer-facing cluster
Formalize rollout checklist for future metric-window changes including load-test signoff
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha: Initial triage concluded probe-gating reduced effective trigger counts during the spike. Started rollback to prior damping settings.
2026-03-11 - Luca: Deployed temporary metric-window extension to 45s for affected endpoints; observed improved scale-up in synthetic bursts.
2026-03-12 - Mei: Prototype of percentile-based KEDA trigger merged to staging for canary testing.
2026-03-13 - Priya: Customer-facing incident summary drafted and sent to account teams for impacted customers. No regulatory/customer data exposure.
2026-03-13 - Luca: Marking ticket Done after action items assigned and initial mitigations validated in staging. Follow-ups scheduled in backlog.
postmortem_notes: Trade-offs: The original change to shorten aggregation windows reduced monitoring costs but reduced fidelity for short bursts. We accepted cost regression to restore a safer default while building adaptive gating. Long-term plan balances cost and reliability via per-endpoint policies.
outcome: Root cause identified as probe-gating + narrower metric window causing false-negative scale decisions. Short-term rollback and metric window increase mitigated recurrence. Medium-term plan is adaptive gating and percentile triggers to improve responsiveness to bursty workloads.
